title-group.article-title: Synthetic fixture: visible-light oxidative chain scission of polystyrene

abstract.p: Under 450 nm blue LEDs and an air atmosphere, polystyrene (PS) was converted to benzoic acid in 40% yield using FeCl3 as a photocatalyst in acetonitrile.

sec.title: Characterization
sec.p: Molar masses were determined by SEC in THF at 35 °C relative to polystyrene standards. Selected samples were also measured with multi-angle light scattering (MALS).

sec.title: Photoreaction
sec.p: PS (Mn = 120 kg mol−1, Đ = 2.1) and 5 mol% FeCl3 in MeCN (0.1 M) were irradiated with a 456 nm Kessil lamp (40 W) under O2 balloon for 24 h at room temperature.

sec.title: Results
sec.p: After irradiation the Mn decreased from 120 to 3.4 kg/mol, while Mw of 250 kDa fell substantially. The dispersity changed from 2.1 to 1.6.
